paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD's loving devotion is what this whole psalm stands on. It opens by saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever," and it closes by telling the wise to "consider the loving devotion of the LORD" (Psalm 107:1, 43). Everything in between is the proof.

Look at the people who needed rescuing. Lost ones, locked-up ones, sick ones, storm-tossed ones. Some were in trouble through their own rebellious ways, and some were just caught out on the deep (Psalm 107:11, 17, 23-26). Every time, the same thing happens: "Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble," and He answers (Psalm 107:6, 13, 19, 28). So when you're in a mess, no matter how you got there, you know where to turn. You don't need a fancy speech, just a cry.

And once He's pulled you out, SAY SO, baker! The psalm tells the redeemed to speak up, to declare His works and to praise Him among the people (Psalm 107:2, 22, 32). Thanks isn't meant to sit quietly in the pantry, friend. So think about where He has met you, and tell somebody this week.
